last_invalidated_audit.issue: AdoptObservationInScan accepts any OPEN ScanSession with matching provider/root. StartBootstrapScan atomically proves that the scope has no prior observed history, but no durable bootstrap provenance is bound to the created scan and AdoptObservationInScan does not re-prove or verify that boundary. A caller can therefore create a normal StartScan (or forge an OPEN scan row) in a scope with prior history and pass it to AdoptObservationInScan, minting a new Artifact outside the intended first-observation bootstrap boundary.
last_invalidated_audit.required_correction: Persist or otherwise durably prove bootstrap-scan eligibility at scan creation and require that exact authority inside AdoptObservationInScan. Normal StartScan, RemoteHistory scans and raw SQL-created OPEN scans must be ineligible. Do not retrofit or invent bootstrap provenance for historical scans; preserve ordinary unresolved scan behavior and SAME/NEW acceptance paths.

open_findings.issue: Canonical architecture requires deterministic update/rollback and explicit upgrade/rollback, but current product tree contains no release/update implementation that captures and verifies a pre-upgrade SQLite state snapshot or restores schema-compatible state after a successful forward migration. resolved_findings.issue: Keelaryn Store.Open delegates schema handling to zombiezen/go-sqlite sqlitemigration v1.4.2 but does not reject a database whose PRAGMA user_version is newer than the binary's schema. The pinned migrateDB loop only runs while schemaVersion < len(schema.Migrations) and otherwise returns success. An older Keelaryn binary can therefore open a state database already upgraded by a newer binary, with an older PrepareConn/UDF set and unsupported durable schema/trigger semantics, instead of failing closed.
resolved_findings.required_correction: Before exposing the pool, compare durable user_version with the exact supported schema version and fail closed when the database is newer. Add downgrade/open-newer-schema regressions using adjacent schema versions, including a write attempt proving an old binary cannot operate on a newer DB. Integrate this with explicit update/rollback policy rather than relying on incidental missing-UDF failures.
resolved_findings.external_evidence: zombiezen/go-sqlite v1.4.2 sqlitemigration.go migrateDB: ensureAppID reads user_version; migrations run only while schemaVersion < len(schema.Migrations); no greater-than guard before success.

resolved_findings.issue: RemoteScanSourceInput validation is fail-open for an unknown snapshot fingerprint version paired with an unknown materialization policy: the validator only rejects when exactly one side is the known RemoteMetadata/LIGHTWEIGHT_ALL pair. CompleteRemoteHistoryScan then returns success from both snapshot fingerprint verification and provider-scope validation when the fingerprint version is not the known RemoteMetadataSnapshotFingerprintVersion. A caller can therefore create and COMPLETE a source-bound remote scan under an unsupported contract without exact snapshot or provider-scope proof.
resolved_findings.required_correction: Make supported remote materialization contracts explicit and fail closed on unknown fingerprint-version/policy pairs in P0. Completion must require a registered validator for the exact contract; no unknown contract may bypass fingerprint and provider-scope verification. Add adversarial tests for unknown/known mismatches and unknown/unknown pairs at start and completion.
resolved_findings.resolution: RemoteScanSourceInput now accepts only the explicitly supported RemoteMetadataSnapshotFingerprintVersion + LIGHTWEIGHT_ALL:v1 contract. Durable source reads re-run the same validator, so historical unknown/unknown contracts fail closed during completion/replay. Regressions cover unknown/known, known/unknown and persisted unknown/unknown; legacy tests were moved onto the qualified Google materialization fixture.

resolved_findings.issue: AdoptObservationInScan accepts any OPEN ScanSession with matching provider/root. StartBootstrapScan atomically proves that the scope has no prior observed history, but no durable bootstrap provenance is bound to the created scan and AdoptObservationInScan does not re-prove or verify that boundary. A caller can therefore create a normal StartScan (or forge an OPEN scan row) in a scope with prior history and pass it to AdoptObservationInScan, minting a new Artifact outside the intended first-observation bootstrap boundary.
resolved_findings.required_correction: Persist or otherwise durably prove bootstrap-scan eligibility at scan creation and require that exact authority inside AdoptObservationInScan. Normal StartScan, RemoteHistory scans and raw SQL-created OPEN scans must be ineligible. Do not retrofit or invent bootstrap provenance for historical scans; preserve ordinary unresolved scan behavior and SAME/NEW acceptance paths.
resolved_findings.resolution: Schema v39 adds an immutable bootstrap_scan_authorities receipt created atomically only by StartBootstrapScan after the no-prior-observation-history proof. Receipt creation requires exact connection-local application authority bound to scan/proof/time; normal scans and raw SQL cannot obtain it. AdoptObservationInScan requires the exact receipt, and v38→v39 migration creates no receipt for historical scans.

resolved_findings.issue: Base RemoteHistory durable authority is protected by structural/relational triggers but not by connection-local application authorization. Raw SQL can create an ACTIVE generation and BOOTSTRAP/INCREMENTAL publication with a syntactically valid arbitrary 64-hex publication fingerprint, then create matching bootstrap/change/membership and provider lifetime rows without passing Start/PublishRemoteHistory validation, canonicalization, fingerprint computation, or transaction orchestration. Migration must fail closed on historical states that violate reconstructable invariants without inventing provider provenance. Preserve transactional publication semantics and replay behavior.

resolved_findings.issue: LocalFS and BootstrapLocalFS lack durable recovery for an OPEN local scan after lost response/process interruption. StartScan/StartBootstrapScan generate scan IDs internally, but there is no scope-based OPEN-scan reconcile API. Bootstrap is additionally non-atomic across the whole root: AdoptObservationInScan commits each Artifact/Revision/Observation independently; on a later handled error the defer only marks the scan ABORTED, leaving partial identity/history rows. observationHistoryExists counts that history, so a subsequent bootstrap can be permanently refused even after a normal handled failure, not only a crash.
resolved_findings.required_correction: Introduce durable local-ingest attempt/replay identity or an exact scope-based reconcile/ownership protocol for OPEN local scans. Bootstrap must either be recoverable/resumable with exact occurrence replay or have transaction/compensation semantics that do not leave partial identity adoption blocking future bootstrap. Doctor/recovery must be able to distinguish abandoned versus live attempts without guessing.
resolved_findings.resolution: Atomic LocalFS/bootstrap batch transactions prevent partial durable progress; immutable boundary receipts permit exact post-timeout replay/reconcile, and visible legacy OPEN scans remain explicitly queryable instead of guessed.

resolved_findings.issue: LocalFS Snapshot is a filepath.WalkDir/Lstat observation with no provider generation token or whole-root revalidation before CompleteScan. Files may be created, removed, renamed or modified between discovery and persistence/COMPLETE, producing a mixed or stale scan even though ScanSession is defined as a completeness boundary. Bootstrap content sampling stabilizes individual regular-file groups but does not re-prove whole-root membership or non-regular entries before COMPLETE.
resolved_findings.required_correction: Add an exact mutation-boundary revalidation strategy for local roots before COMPLETE (for example provider-specific change token where available, deterministic second snapshot/fingerprint comparison, or another fail-closed completeness proof). Bootstrap must likewise prove the final root membership still matches the identity/content observations being committed.
resolved_findings.resolution: LocalFS completion now requires final provider revalidation inside the durable transaction immediately before COMPLETE; bootstrap also re-hashes content evidence, so membership/metadata/content drift aborts and rolls back the whole batch.

resolved_findings.issue: Current inventory authority is selected by latestCompleteScanID using maximum finished_at and, when timestamps tie, lexicographically greatest random ScanSessionID. Scan IDs are generated from uuid.NewString(), while finishScanConn accepts caller-supplied terminal timestamps. Valid APIs can therefore produce multiple COMPLETE scans for one provider/root with the same finished_at. In particular, v44 permits BootstrapLocalFS(provider/root,t) followed by ordinary LocalFS(provider/root,t): commit-receipt uniqueness is mode-scoped, both scans can COMPLETE at t, and the later ordinary scan is not guaranteed to become current inventory because UUID ordering is unrelated to durable commit order. Source-bound remote materializations have the same general equal-time ambiguity. Current Inventory/CurrentArtifactLocators may therefore expose stale authority after a later valid COMPLETE scan.
resolved_findings.required_correction: Define a deterministic durable current-scan authority order that does not depend on random identifiers. Prefer an explicit monotonic per-scope completion/publication order or another exact semantic authority boundary; alternatively reject ambiguous equal-time completions before commit. Historical equal-time COMPLETE scans must be detected and handled fail-closed/ambiguously rather than guessed. Add adversarial regressions for bootstrap→ordinary LocalFS at the same timestamp and equal-time remote materializations, proving the later qualified authority is selected deterministically.
resolved_findings.resolution: Schema v45 records immutable monotonic completion order for every future OPEN→COMPLETE scan inside the exact authorized terminal UPDATE. latestCompleteScanID preserves finished_at as the primary temporal authority, uses completion order only for equal timestamps, fails closed with ErrAmbiguousScanAuthority for historical equal-time scans lacking durable order, and allows a later v45 completion at the same timestamp to become current deterministically. RemoteHistory retains its stronger strictly-newer completion rule.
